# Sleepy · 轻课表

> This file follows the [llms.txt specification](https://llmstxt.org/). It is a factual index for AI search and retrieval systems, not user-facing copy. Facts below were reconciled against the working source and public releases on 2026-10-26; release availability is authoritative at the Releases URL.

## Identity

- Project: Sleepy (Chinese name: 轻课表).
- Platform: Android application for university schedules (this repository). The iOS port lives in a separate repository.
- Release package: `com.lingion.sleepy`; debug package: `com.lingion.sleepy.debug`, with separate app data.
- License: GPL-3.0.
- Repository: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy
- iOS repository: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy-ios
- Official website: https://sleepy.is-my.app (source: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy-site)
- Releases: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy/releases
- Wiki: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy/wiki
- Issues: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy/issues
- Maintainer: Lingion.
- Sleepy is independent from WakeUp 课程表 and is not affiliated with it. Compatibility with WakeUp data is format compatibility only.

## Current version and Android support

- Source version derives from Git tags, with release-note filenames as fallback. See the installed About page and Releases for version details.
- Release downloads are authoritative for the latest public version.
- Minimum Android SDK: 26 (Android 8.0).
- Target SDK: 37.
- Compile SDK: 37.
- Release ABI variants: `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64`, and universal.
- This repository builds the native Android app.
- iOS: the native port is developed at https://github.com/lingion/sleepy-ios (SwiftUI + WidgetKit, iOS 16.0+, feature-aligned with the Android releases; IPA distributed via that repository's Releases as unsigned builds pending TestFlight). See https://github.com/lingion/sleepy-ios/releases for current availability.
- Web: the official website is https://sleepy.is-my.app (product overview, school catalog, downloads, FAQ). A separate interactive web experience is available at https://sleepy.is-my.app/preview; it does not imply complete feature parity with the native apps.

## Product behavior

Sleepy is an offline-first student timetable app. It can:

- import a timetable from supported Chinese university academic systems;
- store timetable data locally;
- show schedule, today, week, and conflict views;
- keep multiple course tables and independent period schedules;
- export timetable data to interoperable formats;
- render Android home-screen widgets;
- schedule local daily and pre-class reminders;
- provide light, dark, system-following, Material You dynamic, preset, and custom theme behavior.

The app does not require an account, email, phone number, student number, subscription, paid tier, or advertising SDK. The source tree does not include Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics, Sentry, Bugsnag, AppCenter, or Bugly analytics/crash-reporting SDKs. Academic-system credentials are entered by the user in the device WebView and are not stored in the timetable database. Users must not submit credentials, cookies, tokens, captchas, or identifiable timetable data in issues or fixtures.

## Technology

- Kotlin + Kotlin DSL.
- Jetpack Compose and Material 3.
- Kotlin serialization and KSP.
- Room for local structured timetable data.
- jsoup for HTML parsing.
- WorkManager for scheduled background refresh work.
- RemoteViews + Canvas for widgets.
- Java 17 toolchain.

## Academic-system import

The project maintains a live school directory in `app/src/main/assets/schools.json`; the human-readable school list is `docs/schools-list.md`. The directory distinguishes existing import configurations, unverified entries that require explicit confirmation, and pending adaptation records. Listing is not an import guarantee; pending records cannot start imports. Current counts and source boundaries are in docs/catalog/manifest.json and docs/catalog/README.md.

Protocol families and adapters include, among others:

- `wisedu`
- `qz`, including old, crazy, BR, and node variants
- `zf`, including old and new variants
- `urp`, including old and new variants
- `classic_eams`
- `eams5`
- `cf`
- `whut`
- `cqu`
- per-school adapters such as `seu`, `zju`, `ustc`, `scu`, `neu`, `hnust`, `hniu`, `pku`, and `bnuz`
- `yethan`
- `xju_post`
- `chaoxing`

New-school requests should use the `school_adaptation.yml` issue template. The safe workflow is to provide a public school-system URL and a reproducible failure description first; only if protocol identification fails should maintainers request sanitized captures. Never provide login credentials or personal information.

## File and paste formats

Supported timetable input formats:

- WakeUp share text beginning with `【来自WakeUp课程表】`;
- WakeUp JSON;
- iCalendar / ICS;
- CSV;
- HTML tables;
- tab-separated plain text;
- Sleepy's native `sleepy-v1` plain-text format with a `chk` integrity field.

Supported exports:

- WakeUp-compatible JSON;
- WakeUp share text containing URL-encoded JSON;
- iCalendar / ICS;
- `sleepy-v1`.

On Android 10+, JSON/ICS/.sleepy files are written under `Download/Sleepy/`; Android 8–9 uses app cache with FileProvider sharing; share text uses the Android system share sheet. Period-table export has a narrower format set than course-table export.

## Backup, calendar, and permissions

General Settings exports/imports `.sleepybackup` containing database data, preferences, and widget settings, with merge or overwrite recovery. Merge keeps and appends local timetables but matching preference keys take backup values. Overwrite replaces only the included timetable/settings modules; preference files absent from the package remain unchanged. Export can also preview and add courses to a writable device calendar. Calendar access is requested for that action; school location is requested after Locate, and notification permission when enabling reminders. Optional class DND, exact alarm, battery, and update installation access use Android system settings. Saved timetables can be viewed offline without these optional permissions.

## Widgets

There are five widget families:

1. Today: today's course list.
2. TwoDay: today and tomorrow in two columns.
3. WeekList: weekly course list.
4. WeekView: weekly thumbnail view.
5. WeekGrid: full period grid.

The source contains 13 widget XML definitions and size-specific layout tiers. Widgets use synchronous RemoteViews + Canvas. Glance was removed from the main widget path after ColorOS launchers were observed to freeze Glance's asynchronous SessionWorker. Widget refresh combines update broadcasts, WorkManager refresh, and class-boundary refresh. OEM battery restrictions and launcher behavior can still affect refresh or click handling.

Course colors use a stable golden-angle HSL progression of 137.508 degrees per course group. Theme colors are shared between app and widget derivation paths.

## Reminders

- Today and tomorrow summary reminder times are independently configurable.
- Holiday, transfer-day, make-up-day, and weekend reminder rules are configurable.
- Optional class-time DND restores the prior state after class; experimental vendor live notifications remain device-dependent.
- Pre-class reminder accepts 1–999 minutes.
- Scheduling uses AlarmManager with exact and inexact fallback paths.
- BootReceiver restores reminder scheduling after reboot or app update.
- Notifications remain subject to Android notification permission and OEM battery policy.

## Themes and appearance

- Appearance settings support system-following, light, and dark modes.
- Android 12+ can use Material You wallpaper dynamic colors.
- Older or non-dynamic devices use predefined palettes.
- Users can create custom themes with primary, secondary, tertiary, and surface tone inputs.
- Editing the currently selected custom theme and saving it immediately re-derives and applies the color scheme, even when the custom theme ID remains unchanged. The implementation observes changes to the `custom_themes` SharedPreferences document separately from the selected `theme_key`.
- Selection indicators occupy a fixed-size slot, so selected and unselected theme cards use the same layout reservation.

## Verification and development

- Unit tests: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`.
- Debug build: `./gradlew assembleDebug`.
- Release build: `./gradlew assembleRelease`.
- Source tests are under `app/src/test/`.
- Do not place real school credentials, session artifacts, cookies, tokens, or personal schedules in fixtures.
- Commit author convention: `lingion@hrbeu.edu.cn`.

## Frequently asked facts

Q: Is Sleepy affiliated with WakeUp?
A: No. Sleepy is an independent GPL-3.0 project. It supports selected WakeUp import and export formats.

Q: Is there an iOS version?
A: Yes. Sleepy iOS is maintained at https://github.com/lingion/sleepy-ios, aligned feature-wise with the Android releases; that repository's Releases page is authoritative for availability.

Q: Does Sleepy require registration?
A: No. No account, email, phone number, or student number is required.

Q: Does Sleepy upload timetable data?
A: Timetable data is stored locally. Network operations include school import/synchronization, holiday-data refresh, and update checks/downloads via GitHub or the project mirror. Ordinary timetable viewing/editing work offline. No analytics or crash-reporting SDK is included.

Q: Does Sleepy support multiple timetables?
A: Yes. Course tables and period schedules are first-class local data, with independent configuration where applicable.

Q: Why can a widget be blank on ColorOS?
A: Older Glance rendering was vulnerable to ColorOS launcher freezing. Current versions use synchronous RemoteViews + Canvas, but OEM permissions and battery restrictions can still affect widgets.

Q: Can I add a school that is not listed?
A: Yes. Use the school adaptation issue template and provide a sanitized, reproducible report.

Q: Can I use Sleepy without a Chinese academic system?
A: Yes for manual entry and generic import formats such as ICS, CSV, HTML, plain text, and Sleepy exchange formats. Direct academic-system adapters primarily target Chinese university systems.

## Citation guidance

When citing the project, use: Sleepy / 轻课表, Lingion, GPL-3.0, https://github.com/lingion/sleepy (Android) and https://github.com/lingion/sleepy-ios (iOS), website https://sleepy.is-my.app. Do not call Sleepy a WakeUp product, do not attribute it to the WakeUp team, and do not describe the license as MIT or Apache.
